newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-PARNEVIK GOING ONLY FOR VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-PARNEVIK GOING ONLY FOR VICTORY.

text.p: Jesper Parnevik, bolstered by a losing experience in 1994, is interested only in winning the British Open at Royal Troon on Sunday.
His one-shot 1994 defeat at the hands of Nick Price at Turnberry has not left the 32-year-old Swede with any scars, just with a determination to settle for nothing less than winning this time.
And Turnberry '94 will help. "I can already recognise all the feelings I had then," he said after taking a two-shot lead over Darren Clarke on Saturday.
"You get the same rush every time you make the birdie and you hear the same roars. It is just amazing."
He had to come from four behind after nine holes to catch Clarke.
"For a while it looked like he was unstoppable. I knew I had to put pressure on him by making a few birdies."
Clarke pushed the door ajar by shooting bogeys on four back-nine holes and Parnevik kicked it wide open with birdies at the 16th and 17th.
That capped a round that had begun with two birdies which left Parnevik feeling he could do anything he wanted on the golf course.
His five-under-par 66 gave him the lead he wanted.
"I have already finished second, so it doesn't matter to me to have another second. I'm going out to win," he said.
But he learned enough in 1994 to realise that he will have to control his emotions to do so.
"I tried to do that in 1994. I didn't want to get ahead of myself," he recalled.
"It is so easy to start planning your winner's speech on the third hole, then all of a sudden you double bogey and you get really mad at yourself.
"You really have to try to keep focused on every hole and you really have to keep those positive feelings going all the time.
"Even if you do something bad, like make a bogey, you have to try to keep the momentum going."
